lacuna.name: bf16-outlier-recast-practice
lacuna.repo_anchor: plan/0005-format-interop/README.md stage 10, quoted: 'BF16 checkpoint adapter: the most commonly hit gate of all: modern releases ship bf16 and sm_75 has no bf16 tensor support (upstream answer: pass dtype=float16). Recast bf16->fp16 at load (8 mantissa bits fit fp16's 10) with an overflow range check: >65504 outliers reported, never silently truncated.' Same README stage 4 names it as prerequisite substrate; sibling result autoround-lowbit-landscape.json dependency_order already records the standing link: 'the stage-10 bf16->fp16 recast, since both target checkpoints ship dtype=bfloat16 and nothing runs on sm75 without it' (Intel/Qwen3.6-27B-int4-AutoRound and Intel/Qwen3.8-27B-bpw2.8-AutoRound, dtype bfloat16 verified config-level in that run, 2026-09-07). Outline item bf16-outlier-recast-practice (category: formats) carries the four leads this research verifies (Unsloth Gemma-3, transformers #39972, arXiv:2510.26788, vLLM v0.11.1).
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the practice landscape is: nobody ships an overflow-audited bf16->fp16 recast; every production path is either warning-only-cast or hard-refusal, and the wild-failure record concentrates in activation-space (Gemma family, vision towers), not weight-space. (1) vLLM practice, verified in-tree at the fork pin (sm75-marlin branch, upstream base 79378fe6e8, v0.28.0-era): pre-Ampere GPUs get supported_dtypes=[fp16,fp32] (vllm/platforms/cuda.py, capability<8.0), an explicit bf16 request raises 'Bfloat16 is only supported on GPUs with compute capability of at least 8.0 ... use --dtype=half', and the auto path recasts with two log lines only - 'Your device ... doesn't support bfloat16. Falling back to float16' (_resolve_auto_dtype) and 'Casting torch.bfloat16 to torch.float16' (_get_and_verify_dtype) - with no value-range audit at any point in the 2.5-year history of that message (present in vllm/config.py since at least 2024-04-26, PR #4326 era). Separately vLLM maintains a hard fp16 blocklist _FLOAT16_NOT_SUPPORTED_MODELS introduced by PR #18751 '[Core] Rework dtype resolution' (merged 2025-06-01) as {gemma2, gemma3, plamo2, glm4} with reason string 'Numerical instability. Please use bfloat16 or float32 instead.' - a ValueError, not a runtime check; gemma3_text joined ~2025-09-05 (embeddinggemma #24318), plamo2 left 2026-07-24 when the model was removed (#49729); pin state: gemma2, gemma3, gemma3_text, glm4. So upstream's entire practice is dtype-policy, never magnitude-policy. (2) transformers' canonical refusal: issue #39972 'Gemma3 with fp16 in inference' (opened 2025-08-06 by DGTell, closed stale 2025-09) - maintainer Rocketknight1 (Matt Gardner), 2025-09-08, verbatim: 'Gemma3 was never intended to be run in fp16 ... Some models, by design, operate in value ranges beyond the fp16 range - recent versions of Pixtral are a good example of this. The vision tower in those models just outputs values >= 1e5 and these often overflow fp16. There's not much you can do about this - a clamp can temporarily fix it, but it will reduce model quality ... If your hardware is too old to support bfloat16, then you should consider doing inference in another framework. For example, you can use llama-cpp.' The reporter's own workaround (unmerged, self-described hack): clamp RMSNorm output and fp32 residual adds to +-65503.9 before .half(). The predecessor #36822 'Gemma 3 is broken with fp16' (2025-03-19) contains the strongest counter-argument, from mobicham: 'the efficient low-bit kernels to run quantized models faster mainly support fp16 not bf16 (because of some limitations related to atomic addition with bf16) - this includes gemlite and Marlin in vllm', with a concrete clipping fix PR #36832 'gemma3 fp16 fix' (clip activations + residual) - closed 2025-07-02 without merge, i.e., the clipping precedent exists and was rejected upstream. (3) Unsloth's Gemma-3 investigation (blog 'Fine-tune Gemma 3', 2025-03-14, and 'Gemma 3 training fixes'): Gemma 3 1B-27B intermediate activations exceed fp16 max 65504; published per-layer chart 'Gemma 3 Huge Activations' (absolute max magnitude vs layer number, dashed line at 65504): the 27B crosses ~65504 around layer ~18-20 and peaks around 6-8e5 (~10-12x fp16 max) [uncertain: values read from the published webp graph, approximate]; 12B plateaus around 3.5-4e5; 4B text states intermediate activations reach up to ~2e5 ('4x larger than FP16's max'); 1B stays below the line. Root cause is the RMSNorm sqrt(hidden)-scaled activations, i.e., activation-space, not weight-space. Unsloth's shipped fix is the selective-precision precedent, not clipping: matmuls in fp16, all intermediate/residual activations kept bf16 (or fp32), layernorms in fp32 - which is why their kernels still run on T4-era fp16-only hardware without NaNs. (4) Wild failure cases with numbers, 2025-2026: vLLM issue #40290 + open PR #40347 '[Bugfix][Gemma4] Fix vision fp16 overflow causing <pad> output' (2026-04-20): Gemma4 SigLIP standardization '(h - std_bias) * std_scale' with |std_bias| reaching ~5.4e4 in the 31B/26B-A4B checkpoints (vision_config.standardize=True); the intermediate saturates to -inf, NaNs through the downstream RMSNorm, and the LM samples <pad> for every image token 'silently, with no warning in vLLM logs' - the closest thing in the record to a near-65504 WEIGHT, and the fix precedent is mixed precision (keep vision_tower bf16, cast pixel_values, convert at the projector boundary via the existing embedding-projection dtype cast). vLLM issue #54377 (2026-08-29, open): Cohere Transcribe on Turing fails engine init because pos_bias_u/v parameters created fp32 never see the model-wide cast - the recast's straggler-class bug, fixed by .to(q.dtype) at use site (open fix #54399 'CohereASR FP16 attention bias dtype'). Pixtral vision towers emit >= 1e5 activations (per the Rocketknight comment above). HF discussion google/gemma-3-27b-it #45 documents repeated/garbled tokens in fp16. By contrast, mainstream Qwen-class fp16 serving on T4/Turing is routine practice (Colab T4 vLLM guides, T4/L4/H100 benchmark write-ups; garbage-token reports for Qwen3.6-27B trace to chat-template/FP8 issues, not the bf16->fp16 cast). (5) Counter-evidence reconciled: arXiv:2510.26788 'Defeating the Training-Inference Mismatch via FP16' (Qi, Liu, Zhou, Pang, Du, Lee, Lin; 2025-10-30) shows uniform FP16 makes RL fine-tuning stable where BF16 collapses (sequence-level training-inference mismatch ~24x smaller under FP16; sanity-task max accuracy 99% FP16 vs 95% BF16+MIS; AIME24 39% vs 34%; BF16 GRPO collapses after ~600 steps, FP16 does not), and handles fp16's range with standard DYNAMIC LOSS SCALING only (scale up, divide gradients, back off on inf detection) while noting 'using FP16 for extremely large models might present engineering challenges related to its limited range'. It argues mantissa precision (10 bits > bf16's 7 effective), not range, is the win - on bf16-capable hardware, orthogonal to the sm75 recast, and in fact it SUPPORTS the recast's core premise that fp16's wider mantissa is fidelity-safe; range remains the only new risk the recast must audit. (6) Outlier-magnitude context from the quantization literature: LLM.int8() (arXiv:2208.07339, 2022) reports emergent outlier activations up to ~70x typical feature dimensions in >=6.7B models - values still far below fp16 max (that problem is int8-grid resolution), confirming that mainstream-LLM weights/activations do not approach 65504; the documented >65504 population is Gemma-family text activations (~2e5-8e5) and vision-tower outputs/biases (>=1e5 activations, ~5.4e4 standardization biases). No mainstream text-LLM checkpoint is reported to ship body weights above 65504 [uncertain: absence of evidence, no systematic survey exists]. (7) llama.cpp practice (the framework transformers points users to): modern convert_hf_to_gguf.py PRESERVES bf16 by default (heuristics: 'detected bfloat16 tensor dtype, setting --outtype bf16'); a forced --outtype f16 goes through a bare data.astype(np.float16) in gguf-py/gguf/quants.py, verified locally: numpy emits only RuntimeWarning 'overflow encountered in cast' and produces inf (so even the check-adjacent behavior is warning-only, and the inf lands silently in the GGUF); per-tensor F32 keep-lists (norms, 1-D tensors) are the practice that makes fp16 GGUF runtimes viable for Gemma-class models because RMSNorm is computed in fp32 upstream of the cast point.
lacuna.sm75_viability: What actually runs on Turing (T4/2080Ti/RTX 6000) today and what the recast must respect. (1) The cast machinery already on the fork's pinned tree: vllm/platforms/cuda.py gates supported_dtypes=[fp16,fp32] below capability 8.0 and raises on explicit bf16; vllm/config/model.py _get_and_verify_dtype performs the config-dtype->run-dtype decision (auto fallback warning, explicit-cast warning, blocklist ValueError). The pin's blocklist is gemma2/gemma3/gemma3_text/glm4 - all hard-refused on ANY hardware in fp16; the operator's Qwen-class targets are outside the blocklist and are the class the community routinely serves in fp16 on T4. (2) The failure modes the audit must catch are silent: torch .to(float16) and numpy astype produce inf with at most a stderr RuntimeWarning (verified locally for numpy; torch is fully silent), and the Gemma4 case shows inf propagating to coherent-looking but wrong output (<pad> per image token) with no log line. The fp32-straggler failure (#54377) is loud (matmul dtype raise at init) but shows the recast must be a model-wide post-load pass, not a per-tensor load hook alone. (3) Engine reality (sibling-verified, turing-engine-upstream-drift.json): between v0.24.0 (2026-06) and the pin, FlashInfer is floored at SM80 upstream (commit cf16db7 in PR #45375, raised pending flashinfer#3620/#3621; regression filed as vLLM #47549 2026-07-03), so upstream releases have no auto-selected sm75 attention backend; restore PR #55380 (open since 2026-09-04) demonstrates the serving target directly on v0.28.0 with 2x RTX 2080Ti 22G: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 with fp16 KV cache passes, unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 with marlin linear backend passes with fp16 and fp8 KV, FlashInfer on sm75 limited to HEAD_DIM<=256 (64 KiB smem; fix flashinfer#3526 shipped in flashinfer v0.6.16). The recast row is engine-independent (it runs at load) and unaffected by that window, but serving e2e needs the fork's retained Turing engine. (4) The fork's concrete prerequisite (sibling-verified NOTE): Intel/Qwen3.6-27B-int4-AutoRound and Intel/Qwen3.8-27B-bpw2.8-AutoRound both declare dtype bfloat16 (their unquantized MTP layers and scale tensors are bf16) - on sm75 nothing of the operator's target class loads without this recast, and the quantized weights themselves are integer-packed (range-free) so the audit surface is the bf16 float tensors only. (5) Expected magnitude safety on the target class: Qwen-family body weights live around O(0.01-0.1) [uncertain: practice-level knowledge, no systematic per-tensor survey published], unscaled activations are far below 65504 (the ~70x outliers of the int8 literature sit orders of magnitude under fp16 max), and the documented overflowers (Gemma text 2e5-8e5 activations, Gemma4 5.4e4 vision bias with large h, Pixtral >=1e5 vision outputs) are all outside the operator's target set; vLLM's blocklist is the upstream codification of exactly that boundary. (6) Precedent semantics available to the fork: report-and-abort (no precedent upstream - would be novel), clipping (preceded by DGTell's hack and mobicham's #36832, both rejected/self-described as quality-reducing - Rocketknight: 'a clamp can temporarily fix it, but it will reduce model quality'), per-channel/per-module rescale or selective precision (preceded by Unsloth's keep-activations-bf16/norms-fp32 recipe, vLLM #40347's keep-tower-bf16-cast-at-projector, llama.cpp's F32 keep-lists, and SmoothQuant/AWQ-style per-channel scale migration from the int8 world) - the only precedents that shipped.

Rocketknight1's canonical 'use another framework' refusal naming Pixtral vision >=1e5. 2025-10-30: arXiv:2510.26788 (FP16 defeats training-inference mismatch; dynamic loss scaling manages range; modern-hardware context). 2025-11-18: vLLM v0.11.1 - the FP16-on-Turing re-enable window: FlashInfer becomes the default CUDA dependency (#26443) and backend selection becomes a priority list (FLASH_ATTN >=8.0 -> FLASHINFER >=7.5 -> TRITON -> FLEX), so Turing auto-selects FlashInfer and community reports FP16 serving working again at large speedup (r/LocalLLaMA Nov 2025); fix = keep tower bf16. 2026-06-23: vLLM PR #45375 (first release v0.24.0) raises the FlashInfer floor to SM80 pending flashinfer#3620/#3621 - the current disable window; regression filed as #47549 (2026-07-03). 2026-07-24: PR #49729 removes plamo2 from the blocklist (model removed). 2026-08-29: #54377 Cohere Transcribe fp16-on-Turing init failure (fp32 stragglers past the model-wide cast); fix #54399 open. 2026-09-04: PR #55380 (open) '[Turing] Restore flashinfer support for SM75' - tested on v0.28.0, 2x 2080Ti, fp16 KV passes; states FlashInfer's sm75 constraints (HEAD_DIM<=256, smem fix in flashinfer v0.6.16 via #3526). Last-good bases for the fork: the pinned v0.28.0-era tree already contains the complete cast+blocklist machinery to extend (vllm/config/model.py, vllm/platforms/cuda.py) and llama.cpp's conversion package is the reference for bf16-preserving defaults + F32 keep-lists; the >65504 audit itself has no upstream implementation to rebase - it is greenfield on this fork.

effort_value.effort_estimate: Adapter-scale, no kernels, roughly one session plus gates. Work items: (1) recast hook in the load path - after dequant/packing of integer tensors, before tensor copy to device: audit every bf16 float tensor with an fp32/fp64 max-|v| reduction, threshold 65504 (fp16 max), emit a structured report (tensor name, count over threshold, max magnitude) and apply policy: default abort with the report, explicit opt-in to per-tensor clamp-to-65504 with the report recorded in the serving config; (2) NaN/Inf passthrough semantics decided and tested (bf16 inf/nan map to fp16 inf/nan; subnormal bf16 values are normal in fp16 - no flush issue); (3) model-wide straggler sweep (post model.to, catch params that never received the cast - the #54377 class); (4) registry row + serving-config record of audit outcome; (5) gate transcript: oracle equality (recast is exact for |v|<=65504 by mantissa-width argument: 8 bits fit in 10) plus the audit report on the two Intel AutoRound targets. Loader-side work only; the kernel ladder, engine, and attention rows are untouched.
effort_value.unlocks: The explicit prerequisite for plan/0005 stages 4 and 13: Intel/Qwen3.6-27B-int4-AutoRound (W4A16) and Intel/Qwen3.8-27B-bpw2.8-AutoRound (W2/W3 mixed) both ship dtype bfloat16 (sibling-verified) - neither loads on sm75 without this recast, so the operator's both-card 27B serving target is gated on this row. More broadly: every bf16 checkpoint in the Qwen/Llama class becomes loadable on T4/2080Ti/RTX6000 with an attested-no-silent-inf guarantee no upstream release provides (vLLM warns and casts blindly; transformers refuses; llama.cpp converts with a numpy RuntimeWarning at best). It also un-gates any future bf16-shipping format row (FP8 checkpoints whose scales/dequant metadata are bf16, MTP draft layers left at 16-bit, etc.) without per-format rework.
effort_value.dependency_order: Repo-internal: needs only the stage-1 checkpoint-adapter load hook (already the substrate for the AutoRound rows) - otherwise independent and can land FIRST; stages 4 (AutoRound adapters) and 13 (both-card 27B target) are hard-blocked on it; the engine row (stage 11) is orthogonal (the recast runs at load, before any attention backend is consulted) so work proceeds in parallel. External: none - torch/numpy provide the casts; the audit is a pure reduction. The fp32-straggler sweep should coordinate with the engine row's model-loading path (same load sequence) to avoid duplicate sweeps. Optional later, explicitly out of scope now: activation-space guards for Gemma-class models (upstream blocklist territory).
effort_value.risk_notes: (1) Silent-inf default everywhere: torch .to(float16) is silent and numpy astype emits only a catchable RuntimeWarning - the audit MUST run on the bf16 bits before any cast, and the policy must be fail-closed (abort) rather than relying on warning visibility. (2) Range vs fidelity must not be conflated: bf16->fp16 is mantissa-lossless (8 effective bits into 10; round-to-nearest-even is exact when the exponent fits), so the ONLY weight-space failure is >65504 (or <2^-24 flush-to-zero, irrelevant for LLM scales); activation-space overflow is a separate, model-class property (Gemma family, vision towers) that the recast neither causes nor fixes - reporting that distinction in the audit output prevents misattribution. (3) Clipping has negative precedents: mobicham's transformers PR #36832 (closed unmerged) and DGTell's clamp hack; maintainer position: 'a clamp can temporarily fix it, but it will reduce model quality' - so clamp must be an explicit, recorded opt-in, never the default. (4) Straggler risk: parameters created fp32 outside the standard load path (Cohere pos_bias_u/v, #54377) survive a model-wide cast and fail loudly later or silently corrupt - the post-cast sweep is part of this row's correctness, not polish. (5) Upstream drift exposure: the fp16 blocklist is a moving list (glm4 added 2025-06, plamo2 added/removed 2026-07) - the fork must rely on its own magnitude audit rather than mirroring the list, and re-run the audit on every checkpoint revision (Intel's bpw2.8 target was updated 2026-08-24). (6) Numerics-risk transfer: inf weights would surface as NaN activations -> garbage tokens with no log line (Gemma4 <pad> precedent) - the row's value is precisely converting that silent class into a load-time refusal. (7) Weight-magnitude claims for the target class (no >65504 body weights expected) are practice-derived, not verified per-tensor this run [uncertain: config-level reads only, per the item's constraint; the audit itself is the verification step].
effort_value.determinism_class: The recast and audit are pure elementwise/reduction functions of the checkpoint bits with no ordering freedom in the result: each bf16 value maps to exactly one fp16 value (exact while |v|<=65504; deterministic inf decision above), and max-|v| reduction is associative and rounding-free, so the audit is bitwise identical run-to-run, restart-to-restart, and single- vs multi-threaded. No atomics, no split-K, no timing inputs; the float64-oracle gate is trivially satisfied for in-range values (oracle equals recast output exactly) and the gate transcript should additionally record the audit report (tensor, count, max) as the artifact. The only nondeterminism the row touches is downstream (engine atomics/split-K per the standing tp2 findings) and is unchanged by this row; median-of-N discipline carries over untouched since the recast adds zero variance.

decision.priority_signal: For doing this next: it is the cheapest row in the milestone (loader-only, one session), it is the recorded hard prerequisite of the operator's two exact target checkpoints (both ship bf16, sibling-verified), and it is the only row whose upstream counterpart permanently refuses to exist (vLLM: warning-only cast for 2.5+ years plus a growing blocklist; transformers: 'use another framework'; llama.cpp: preserve-bf16 default, warning-only when forced) - so the fork's audited recast is differentiating, not redundant. The failure class it guards is the worst kind: silent (inf -> NaN -> plausible-looking wrong tokens; Gemma4 emitted <pad> for every image token with zero log lines), which is exactly what the house oracle-gate discipline exists to exclude. The arXiv:2510.26788 counter-evidence resolves in the recast's favor: it demonstrates fp16's mantissa advantage is real (24x smaller train/infer mismatch) with range handled by standard dynamic scaling - i.e., fp16 is not a degraded legacy format, it is a legitimate target whose only admission price is the range audit this row implements. Against: every practice signal says the audit will return zero outliers on the Qwen-class targets (weights O(0.01-0.1), no >65504 body-weight report anywhere in the literature), so the row is insurance rather than an enabler for the immediate target; and the temptation to extend into Gemma-class fp16 serving should be resisted - upstream's refusal is evidence-based (2e5-8e5 activations need per-module rescale, a different campaign). Window: not window-limited (load-path row, independent of the FlashInfer sm75 flux), but its consumers (stages 4/13) are waiting on it, so sequencing it first costs nothing and unblocks two rows.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0, oracle-first, no timing until numerics are proven, one session. (1) Bit-exactness step (CPU only): synthetic bf16 pattern battery - exponent sweep across the 2^15/2^16 boundary, +-largest-finite-bf16, +-inf, quiet/signaling NaN, subnormals - assert the recast equals a float64 decode-oracle elementwise for |v|<=65504 and that every |v|>65504 value lands in the audit report (count, tensor, max), never silently in a weight tensor; assert numpy-warning and torch-silent behaviors are bypassed (audit runs pre-cast). (2) Real-checkpoint audit step (loader-side, on the fork's own hardware, config-level provenance only): load Intel/Qwen3.6-27B-int4-AutoRound and Intel/Qwen3.8-27B-bpw2.8-AutoRound through the recast hook, record the full per-tensor audit table into the gate transcript - expected result: zero >65504 outliers (if nonzero, STOP and report; that is the row's designed refusal, and it would be a first-in-the-wild datum). (3) Straggler sweep step: after model-wide cast, assert no parameter or buffer retains dtype float32/bfloat16 on the target models (the #54377 class). (4) E2e numerics step (single card, timing forbidden): serve the W4A16 target with the recast active and compare greedy-decode tokens plus final-layer logits (max-abs-diff and cosine vs the float32-upcast run of the same checkpoint on the same card - fp32 is the in-host oracle since bf16-on-sm80 is unavailable) - differences must be attributable solely to fp16 rounding, not range. Timing and the both-card run are stage-13 work, gated on this transcript.
